FIVE ROOT CAUSES, not 82 suppressions. Nothing was silenced with `type: ignore`.

1. `type` IS A FIELD ATTRIBUTE, so `type[BaseModel]` inside a Field class body
   resolves to `Field.type` -- a `str` -- and mypy reports "Variable
   odoo.orm.fields.base.Field.type is not valid as a type" and then treats the
   whole parameter as `Any`. Twelve signatures across seven files read that way,
   which is worse than an error: every call site was unchecked. `_typing.py`
   gains `type ModelClass = type[BaseModel]`, resolved at module scope where
   `type` is the builtin. `metaclass.py` immediately reported a real
   consequence -- `field.__set_name__(cls, name)` passes a `MetaModel`, which
   nothing had been checking.

2. `Field` IS A DESCRIPTOR, so a class attribute DECLARED as `Field` is read
   through `Field.__get__` and written through `Field.__set__`. `related_field:
   Field | None` therefore typed every read as `Any | None` -- the precision was
   already gone -- and every write as an error against `__set__(self, records:
   BaseModel, ...)`. Declared `typing.Any`, which is what `_field_stubs.py`
   already says for `inherited_field`; base.py said `Field | None` for the same
   attribute, so the two disagreed.

3. `_args__` was `dict | None` and no caller has ever tested it for None. It is
   a `ReadonlyDict` from `__init__` onward and is popped off the instance after
   setup, which the class default served. `Mapping[str, Any]` with an empty
   `ReadonlyDict` default says the same thing without the branch nobody takes.

4. `__and__` and `__or__` on the three Domain classes were annotated
   `-> Domain | type[NotImplemented]`. `NotImplemented` is a value, not a type,
   so that annotation is not merely redundant -- mypy rejects it outright
   ("Variable builtins.NotImplemented is not valid as a type") and every
   `domain |= ...` in the tree inherited the fallout. `-> Domain` is the
   correct annotation; mypy special-cases `return NotImplemented`.

5. Four members were reachable at runtime and undeclared on the stub surfaces:
   `Field.related_attrs`, `Field._update_inverse`, and `_ModelStubs`
   `_validate_computed` plus `_compute_field_value`, whose stub signature was
   missing the `validate` parameter the real one takes and every caller passes.

TWO REAL DEFECTS SURFACED, both now raising where they used to confuse:

  - `setup_related` walked a dotted path assigning `model_name =
    field.comodel_name` with no check that the hop is relational. A
    non-relational field mid-path made the next `pool[None]` raise KeyError
    naming a model that was never asked for. It now names the field and the
    segment that cannot be reached through it.
  - `update_db_column` and `_convert_db_column` indexed `self.column_type[1]`
    on a `tuple | None`. Only `update_db` guards it, one frame up. Both now
    say so.

`resolve_depends` also took `registry` as a parameter and then reached the same
object as `Model.pool`; it reads the parameter now, which is what moved
`Registry` accesses in Layer 1 from 30 to 29 -- a doc figure, updated in
module.md and risks.md together with the sentence the doc gate pins.

Measured per section 9.3: fresh venv, mypy==2.3.0 alone, `--no-incremental`, over
an rsync copy of the tree.

test_orm` installed together, 0 failed of 4890 tests.
